# Packages published in the self-hosted opkg repo but NOT installed in the
# image, so users can `opkg install` them on demand.
#
# Why they are not in the image:
#   - size. OpenClash alone pulls ruby, haproxy and dnsmasq-full; the trimmed
#     image is 43 MB and these would roughly double it.
#   - TTL. OpenClash installs its own redirect rules that can bypass the
#     nftables chain byte-ttl owns, and TTL 64 is the point of this firmware.
#     Installing it is a deliberate user choice, not a default.
#
# Dependencies are listed explicitly because the repo is filtered against the
# image manifest: these packages are absent from it, so opkg would not pull
# their dependencies in automatically. The list is the transitive closure of
# every root below, derived from the built .ipk control files - not a guess.
#
# One package name per line. Blank lines and # ignored.

# --- AdGuard Home ---
adguardhome
luci-app-adguardhome

# --- banIP ---
banip
luci-app-banip

# --- SmartDNS ---
smartdns
luci-app-smartdns

# --- iptables-nft shim -----------------------------------------------------
# mwan3, sqm-scripts, nikki and OpenClash all shell out to iptables at
# runtime (mwan3 49 references, OpenClash 362, nikki 16), so they cannot work
# without it. We ship the nft-backed shim, NOT legacy iptables:
#
#   iptables-nft  PROVIDES=iptables, DEFAULT_VARIANT=1, and every binary it
#                 installs is *-nft (iptables-nft, iptables-nft-restore, ...)
#   xtables-nft   DEPENDS=kmod-nft-compat + libnftnl - it writes nft rules
#
# So this is nftables under an iptables-compatible name, which keeps
# firewall4 and the TTL chain intact. xtables-legacy is never pulled in.
iptables-nft
ip6tables-nft
ip6tables-mod-conntrack-extra-nft
ip6tables-mod-ipopt-nft
iptables-mod-conntrack-extra-nft
iptables-mod-ipopt-nft
ipset
kmod-ipt-ipset
kmod-ipt-core
kmod-nft-compat

# --- SQM (traffic shaping) ---
# The cake/hybrid qdiscs are pure tc and contain zero iptables calls; only
# simple.qos uses iptables, for ingress policing. The iptables-nft shim above
# covers that too, so every SQM mode works.
kmod-ifb
kmod-sched-cake
luci-app-sqm
sqm-scripts
tc

# --- mwan3 (multi-WAN failover) ---
mwan3
luci-app-mwan3

# --- Nikki (mihomo) ---
# nikki depends on "mihomo"; the feed's mihomo-meta package provides it.
luci-app-nikki
mihomo-meta
nikki
yq

# --- HomeProxy (sing-box) ---
luci-app-homeproxy
sing-box
firewall4
ucode-mod-digest

# --- OpenClash (clash) ---
luci-app-openclash
haproxy
ruby
ruby-yaml
libncursesw6
dnsmasq-full
bash
curl
ca-bundle
ip
ip-full
kmod-dummy
kmod-inet-diag
kmod-netlink-diag
kmod-nft-tproxy
kmod-tun
unzip
coreutils-nohup
ucode
